title: Lystrosaurus
summary: Lystrosaurus was a heavily built, herbivorous dicynodont therapsid that famously survived the end-Permian mass extinction and became the overwhelmingly dominant land vertebrate of the Early Triassic, comprising up to 90 percent of terrestrial vertebrate individuals in some fossil assemblages. Equipped with a turtle-like beak, rooting tusks, and burrowing adaptations, its cosmopolitan fossils across South Africa, Antarctica, India, and China provided crucial early evidence for the past connection of Pangaea.

uncertainty.note: Genus spans from the Late Permian (Daptocephalus Assemblage Zone, c. 254 Ma) through the Early Triassic (Lystrosaurus Assemblage Zone, ending c. 247 Ma in the Olenekian).

when.display: c. 254–247 Ma (Late Permian to Early Triassic)

where.modern_name: Karoo Basin (Bethulie District, Free State, South Africa; reference area for the Lystrosaurus Assemblage Zone)

importance.justification: Lystrosaurus is the iconic survivor taxon of the end-Permian mass extinction, dominating Early Triassic continental ecosystems and providing classic fossil evidence supporting continental drift.
